transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I suppose occupational health sent me because... well, I’ve gotten into this pattern at work. I'm a biological scientist, and during long lab runs or when I'm prepping for an exhibition, I just push breakfast and lunch aside. And then, by the time I actually do sit down to eat, I just keep it to something very small and controlled. They seemed concerned about it.
Do you try to limit your food intake to control your weight?

Yes, I do. It's... well, if the scale goes up even a fraction, I feel this sharp panic. It just feels like I’m losing the discipline I’ve worked so hard to maintain. So keeping my food intake small is definitely a way to make sure my weight stays exactly where I need it to be.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Yes, I have. My clothes are definitely looser now, and... well, the numbers on the scale have just kept drifting down. Honestly, part of me sees that as a sign that I’m staying focused. It feels like proof that I'm not letting all the chaos at work spill over into my own body.
Do you often think about the possibility of gaining weight?

Yes, constantly. Like I mentioned a moment ago, the idea of the scale going up even a tiny bit brings on this really sharp panic. It's always in the back of my mind. Gaining weight would mean I'm losing that discipline I've built up, so... yes, I think about it pretty much all the time.
Do you ever eat an amount of food that you consider excessive in a short period of time?

No, I don't really do that. My focus is always on keeping my intake as small and controlled as possible, so... no, eating a large amount of food at once isn't something that happens. I'm too careful for that.
Have you ever eaten an amount of food that you considered excessive in a short period of time, even if it's not a regular occurrence?

No, I really haven't. Like I just mentioned, I don't let myself lose control like that. Even as a rare occurrence or a one-off... it just doesn't happen. I keep everything very measured and calculated. The idea of eating a large volume of food all at once is just completely contrary to how I operate.
Have you ever felt like you lost control while eating?

No, not at all. Like I was just saying, my eating is very structured. Control is... well, it's the main focus for me. I always know exactly what I'm consuming and how much, so I've never had a moment where I felt out of control or like I couldn't stop.
Do you ever make yourself vomit or use laxatives after eating?
No, I don't do either of those things. Since I strictly limit what I eat in the first place, there isn't really a need to try and get rid of it afterward. So, no, no vomiting or laxatives.
Do you think you are currently underweight?

I know other people have expressed concern about it, but... I honestly think they're overstating the situation. I mean, I'm still functioning perfectly well. I go to work, I'm still doing all my experiments in the lab, and keeping up with my usual schedule. So, no, I don't feel like my weight is at a level that's medically dangerous.
Is your fear of gaining weight related to a fear of losing control or is it more about the appearance or other concerns?

It's definitely about control. I mean, my work in the lab requires such precision, and I guess I apply that same standard to myself. If the scale goes up even a fraction of a pound, I feel this sharp panic... like I'm losing the discipline I've worked so hard to maintain. It's not really about looking a certain way, it's just about knowing I can manage my own body.
Have you experienced any changes in your menstrual cycle?
No, I haven't noticed any changes. My cycle has always been fairly regular, and... well, it still is. So, no issues there.
How much weight have you lost over the past few months?

I'm not entirely sure of the exact number. I mean, I weigh myself regularly to make sure it isn't going up, but I haven't really kept a running total of what I've lost overall over the past few months. So, I don't really know exactly.
Have you had any menstrual periods in the past three months?
Yes, like I said just a moment ago, my periods have been completely normal. I've had them regularly over the past three months.
Would you say your current weight is more than 15% below the normal weight range for your height?

I haven't calculated the exact percentage, to be honest. But... my clothes are definitely looser, and the numbers on the scale have just kept drifting down. 

I don't really see it as a bad thing, though. Part of me sees that as a sign that I’m focused. It's like... it proves I'm not letting the chaos at work spill over into my body. So I'm just keeping things under control.
Do you currently weigh less than 85% of the normal weight range for someone of your height?

I think that's essentially what you just asked me. Like I said, I haven't calculated the exact percentages. I know my weight is down, but I really don't know if it's below 85 percent of whatever is considered the normal range. I just haven't run those numbers.
Has your weight loss been so significant that others have noticed and commented on it?

Not really, no. I mean, my colleagues at the lab are usually pretty focused on their own work. If anyone has noticed, they haven't actually said anything to me about it. Plus, I usually just wear a lab coat over my clothes during the day anyway, so I don't think it's something that really stands out to anyone else.
Have you had any changes in the heaviness or lightness of your menstrual flow over the past few months?

No, I haven't really noticed any changes like that. My periods have just stopped entirely. I haven't had one in... a few months now, actually. So there isn't really a flow to be heavy or light anymore.
Have you ever felt like you've eaten an amount of food that's larger than what most people would eat in a short period of time?
No, not at all. I actually eat very little. I've never had a time where I felt like I was eating a large amount of food like that.
Do you think your weight loss has had any impact on your overall health?

No, I don't think so. I know people might be concerned, but I honestly think they’re overstating it. I mean, I’m still functioning just fine. I'm still going in and doing my experiments every day, keeping up with my work. So... I just don’t feel like this is medically dangerous or really impacting my health.
How many months has it been since your last menstrual period?
I'm not exactly sure, to be honest. I haven't really been keeping track of the exact number of months. It's just been a while since I had one.
